about: The vocabulary half of #243. This file is normative: docs/agriculture/CAPABILITY_TAXONOMY.md explains it in prose, and agronaut_agent/tests/test_agriculture_capability_taxonomy.py fails if the two drift apart or if a row stops being justified. Two separate axes, because a production system and a water-delivery method answer different questions: 'where do the roots live and what feeds them' versus 'how does water reach the field'. Conflating them is the failure mode #243 was filed to prevent.

production_system.question: Where do the roots live, and what supplies their nutrients?

irrigation_method.question: How is water delivered to a soil-grown root zone?
irrigation_method.scope_note: This axis describes field irrigation of a soil root zone. Soilless systems do not irrigate in this sense: their water delivery is the system type already modelled in aqua_model/system_types.py (raft, nft, media_bed, vertical_tower), and a nutrient solution reaching a substrate or a bare-root channel is not an irrigation method. The one real exception is drip to a substrate, which is recorded as conditional on both soilless rows.

vocabulary.definition: Fish and plants in one recirculating loop: fish waste is the nutrient source, a biofilter converts ammonia to nitrate, and the plant bed is the nutrient sink. The water is shared, so fish-safe chemistry constrains every plant-side decision.
Plants in a soilless medium or water culture fed from a prepared nutrient solution. No fish, so no fish-safe ceiling on nutrient concentration or on the additives that may be used.

Plants rooted in field or potting soil. The soil is a nutrient and water store, so irrigation schedules interact with soil texture, depth and existing water content in a way that solution culture does not.
Water applied at low pressure through emitters to a localized root zone. Wets part of the soil surface, not the canopy.
Water sprayed over the canopy and soil surface. Wets foliage, so application timing, evaporation loss and foliar disease pressure are part of the method, not an afterthought.
Water delivered over the soil surface by gravity: furrows, basins or flooding. Application depth is set by inflow and time, not by an emitter or a spray pattern.
No applied water: the crop is supplied by precipitation only, so a deficit is a scheduling option expressed as a risk rather than a valve setting.

compatibility.reason: Conditional, and only for a substrate: drip to a substrate is real in aquaponics as Dutch buckets for tomato and cucumber, fed after solids removal, so the emitters deliver fish-culture water to a solid bed where the bed does the biofiltration. The delivery system itself is the aquaponics system type (aqua_model/system_types.py), not a field irrigation method. Not supported where the emitter would carry unsettled solids into a bare-root channel. The support decision is ours; no source in the registry covers aquaponic drip delivery.

Not applicable: this method describes field irrigation of a soil root zone, and a soilless system does not irrigate in that sense. Its water delivery is the system type already modelled in aqua_model/system_types.py (raft, nft, media_bed, vertical_tower).

Conditional, and only for a substrate: drip to rockwool, coco or a Dutch bucket is standard hydroponics, with the nutrient solution fed to a solid bed rather than to a bare-root channel. The delivery system itself is the hydroponics system type (aqua_model/system_types.py), not a field irrigation method. The support decision is ours; no source in the registry covers substrate drip.

Not applicable: this method describes field irrigation of a soil root zone, and a soilless system does not irrigate in that sense. Aeroponic misting inside a closed chamber is the system type's own delivery, not a field method. The delivery is the system type already modelled in aqua_model/system_types.py (raft, nft, media_bed, vertical_tower).

Flood-and-drain is the system type's own bookkeeping, not a field surface method. The delivery is the system type already modelled in aqua_model/system_types.py (raft, nft, media_bed, vertical_tower).

Supported as the method to model first, because it is the case FAO-56's water-balance procedure fits most cleanly: a localized wetted fraction, a known application depth, and a schedule expressed in mm. The procedure itself is registered; the worked reference case for it is not written yet (#243 item 3), so no number from it may be presented as verified.
Supported, with the evaporation and foliar-wetting losses carried explicitly rather than buried in an efficiency factor. Awaiting the same reference case as the drip row.
Supported, with application depth set by inflow and duration. Awaiting the same reference case as the drip row.

Supported as the zero-applied-water baseline: the same water balance with irrigation set to zero, which makes a deficit a stated risk rather than a silent assumption. Awaiting the same reference case as the drip row.

capability_statuses.definition: Advice that points at a named source passage. It says what the source says and nothing about this project's own arithmetic.
required_evidence: a registry entry whose locator names a section, table or equation
a verification level recorded for that entry
capability_statuses.available_scope: the whole knowledge corpus, per docs/dpg/CORPUS.md
capability_statuses.must_not_claim: that the guidance was checked against a real system

capability_statuses.definition: A number this project computed and can reproduce: the inputs, the equation and the arithmetic are all on the record, and a reference case pins the expected value with a tolerance.
required_evidence: a registry entry with an equation-level or table-level locator
a worked reference case with expected value and stated tolerance
a test that recomputes the case and fails outside the tolerance
capability_statuses.available_scope: aquaponic sizing only (aqua_model, cited coefficients). Nothing irrigation-side qualifies yet.
capability_statuses.must_not_claim: that the calculation matches any specific field

capability_statuses.definition: A modelled scenario whose parameters are fitted or assumed rather than measured on the system in question. Useful for comparing options, not for predicting an outcome.
required_evidence: every parameter traceable to a registry entry or an explicit assumption
a stated sensitivity to the assumed parameters

capability_statuses.definition: A recommendation shown to hold on a real system under recorded conditions, with the data to prove it.
required_evidence: pilot data collected under the protocol below
the same reference case recomputed against the measured outcome
a named region, season and operator decision record
capability_statuses.available_scope: not available. Agronaut has no field trial, no partner system and no measured irrigation outcome, so this status must not be claimed anywhere in the product.
capability_statuses.must_not_claim: nothing — reaching this status is the claim

pilot_data_protocol.about: What a pilot must record before any result may be described as field-validated. The point is that the quantities below are the minimum needed to recompute a reference case against reality; a pilot that records output only cannot settle anything.
required_fields: site: latitude, longitude, altitude, and soil texture class
season: sowing or transplant date and the crop cycle covered
weather: daily Tmax, Tmin, relative humidity, wind speed at 2 m, and solar radiation or sunshine hours, with the instrument and its height
water applied: method, date, depth in mm, and the source of the water
crop: cultivar, and the measured yield in kg per unit area
operator decisions: every deviation from the schedule, with the reason given at the time
pilot_data_protocol.must_record_when_missing: a missing required field is recorded as missing with its cause, never back-filled from a default
excluded_claims: no field-validation claim may be derived from data that omits any required field
no regional recommendation may be generalised from a single site
